_comment: Which voice speaks each line of the dialogues in data.js, and how each TTS
backend is asked for it. Words are NOT synthesised — they are native Lingua
Libre recordings or nothing, and tools/build_audio.py still owns them. This
file covers sentences only, which no single-word recording can ever supply.
A dialogue names its characters in `sp`, so each character gets its own
voice and a conversation sounds like two people rather than one reading a
script. The monologues carry no `sp`; `texts` assigns them a narrator.
Voice fields:
ref           WHICH REFERENCE CLIP THIS CHARACTER'S VOICE IS CLONED FROM,
by name, from the pool in `references` below. Both backends
use it, so a character sounds like the same person whichever
model reads the line. `--list-voices` prints the pool.
ref_text      Transcript of that clip, if the pool does not carry one.
Optional: OmniVoice runs Whisper over the clip when it is
missing, which works but repeats per line.
gender        male | female. Only a fallback now — it is what builds the
OmniVoice voice-design instruct for a character with no
`ref`, and see `_why_ref` for why you do not want that.
instruct      OmniVoice voice-design string, overriding the one built from
`gender` + `dialect`. Ignored when `ref` is set.
_why_ref: Every character has a `ref` because voice design could not hold an accent.
OmniVoice invents a speaker per call: `instruct: "female"` is not a voice,
it is a filter, and each of the 27 female lines got a different woman — with
a different regional accent. The first listening pass caught ج read as an
Egyptian [g] in خمسة/إجي on some lines and a Levantine [ʒ] on others, from
one model, inside one dialogue. Since the instruct vocabulary contains no
Arabic dialect (see _dialect_note), there is no attribute that says
"Levantine" and nothing to correct it with.
Cloning fixes the speaker, and the accent comes with the speaker. It also
makes the per-character mapping real rather than nominal: before this, سامر
was not one voice across his five lines, he was five different men who
_references_note: The reference voices, borrowed from leva-tts's repo — ten clips, five male
and five female, fetched without its 5.6 GB checkpoint. leva-tts itself was
rejected on a listening pass, but its reference speakers are Levantine and
serve fine as cloning targets for OmniVoice, which synthesises far better.
Set `dir_local` to a path in this repo instead to use your own clips: 3-10
seconds of connected speech each, named for the voice.
_dialect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and appended to the OmniVoice instruct when set.
OmniVoice's upstream README advertises Arabic dialect attributes for voice
design ("Egyptian Lahgtna, Saudi Lahgtna, etc."), but the v2 checkpoint
rejects them: its instruct vocabulary is closed and holds none. Setting this
to "Palestinian Lahgtna" failed every line with
ValueError: Unsupported instruct items found in male, Palestinian Lahgtna
The whole accepted English vocabulary, as the model reports it:
child, teenager, young adult, middle-aged, elderly
very low pitch, low pitch, moderate pitch, high pitch, very high pitch
american, australian, british, canadian, chinese, indian, japanese,
So the dialect cannot travel through the instruct. The hope was that it
would come from the fine-tune and from the Levantine text being read; the
listening pass showed it does not, reliably — see `_why_ref`. Voices are
cloned from reference clips instead, and this field stays empty.
_speed: Under 1.0 because these are A1 listening texts. Slow enough to follow, not
so slow that the prosody stops sounding like speech — the old browser-TTS
_voices_note: `ref` names a clip from the pool: Amina, Badr, Fadi, Fatma, Haneen, Lamyaa,
Mohamed, Mona, Rami, Saad — five male, five female. Run `synth_lines.py
--backend omnivoice --list-voices` to print what the pool currently holds.
Eleven characters share ten clips, so one repeats. What must never repeat is
two characters inside the SAME text: the cafe has two men talking to each
other and the phone call has two women, and a dialogue where both parties
sound identical is worse than no audio. Amina therefore covers both ليلى
(intro) and الراوية (myday), which never appear together.
_texts: Narrator for the texts that are monologues rather than dialogues. Naming
them here rather than defaulting keeps the two from sounding like the same
